headline: Government Confirms All These Simultaneous Outages Are Completely Unrelated
subheadline: *Nation reassured that email, flights and the NSA failing at once is officially just a vibes-based explanation.*
author: Marguerite Hollis, Cybersecurity & Coincidence Desk
seoTitle: Rubio: US Outages Unrelated, Officially Just a Coincidence
seoDescription: Satire: After email, flights and the NSA all went down at once, Washington confirmed the outages are unrelated and US tech strategy is now 'vibes'.
sourceEvent: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was 'zero' information that a cascade of service outages across the country were related to each other or to a malign actor. The outages, which shut down corporate email and grounded thousands of flights, extended to the National Security Agency on Tuesday, disrupting classified communications.

social.x: BREAKING: Washington confirms the email outage, the flight outage and the NSA outage are three separate coincidences travelling together for safety. 'Zero' information they are linked, which is also the amount of information available. Full report:

altHeadlines: Nation's Technology Strategy Updated to 'Probably Fine', Laminated for Durability
NSA Outage Declared No Risk as Secrets Technically Cannot Leave the Building

body:
WASHINGTON — The United States government on Tuesday offered its most comprehensive assessment yet of the week-long cascade of technology failures, confirming there is "zero" information suggesting the outages are connected, and asking Americans to consider the total absence of an explanation a form of reassurance.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters there was "zero" evidence the disruptions — which have grounded thousands of flights, severed corporate email, and on Tuesday reached the National Security Agency's classified communications — were related to each other or to a malign actor. Officials later clarified that "zero" referred not merely to the quantity of evidence but to the government's preferred posture going forward.

"We have looked into it thoroughly," said a senior administration official, speaking on condition of anonymity because the briefing room's video link had failed. "And we can confirm that everything breaking at the same time is simply a statistical coincidence, much like a flock of geese, or a row of dominoes, which famously fall at random."

The assurance marks the formal adoption of what officials describe as the nation's vibes-based continuity strategy, under which simultaneous failures across aviation, communications and the intelligence community are classified as "unrelated pending the discovery of a signed confession".

Government sources stressed the NSA outage posed no security risk, noting that classified material which cannot be transmitted is, by several definitions, the most secure it has ever been. "You cannot leak what cannot leave the building," explained one analyst. "In a sense, the outage is the firewall."

Airlines, meanwhile, welcomed the confirmation that the email outage, the flight outage and the spy agency outage were three separate coincidences travelling together for safety. A carrier spokesperson said grounded passengers had been informed their delays were caused by "independent, unrelated chaos, arriving in formation".

"At first I was worried," said local man Dennis Kowalchuk, 52, whose bank, inbox and boarding pass all stopped working within the same hour. "But then the government explained it was nothing, comprehensively, and I felt this enormous sense of nothing."

Critics alleged the national cyber-response handbook consists of a single page reading "probably fine". The administration pushed back firmly, revealing the handbook is in fact two pages, the second of which says "don't be weird about it".

At press time, officials were forced to end the assurance briefing early after the podium microphone, the teleprompter and the livestream failed simultaneously — incidents a spokesperson recorded as the eleventh, twelfth and thirteenth unrelated coincidences of the day and, statistically, "a pretty good run".
